ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure 13, on the left side of the dashed line OO′ there is a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the paper surface outward, the magnitude of the magnetic induction intensity is B, the convex wire frame abcdefgh rotates uniformly with the dashed line OO′ as the axis at angular velocity ω, abch is a square with side length L, defg is a square with side length L/2, the total resistance of the wire frame is R, and timing starts from the position shown in the figure. During the process of rotating through 90°, what is the law of variation of the instantaneous value i of the induced current in the wire frame with time t?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a vertical dashed line labeled OO′, serving as the rotation axis of the wire frame, and beside it a rotation arrow of angular velocity ω is drawn. Black dots are distributed on the left side of the dashed line, indicating a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the paper surface outward; there are no magnetic-field dots on the right side of the dashed line. The wire frame is convex: on the left side is a large square labeled a, b, c, h, with its right boundary close to the dashed line OO′; on the right side it is connected to a small square labeled d, e, f, g, located on the right side of the dashed line. Then reason: Starting timing from the position shown in the figure, let the angle through which the wire frame has rotated be θ=ωt. Since the magnetic field is only on the left side of OO′, during the process of rotating through 90°, the large square abch is always on the side with magnetic field, while the small square defg is always on the side without magnetic field, so only the large square contributes to the magnetic flux. The area of the large square is L^2, and after rotation the angle between its area vector and the magnetic-field direction is θ, so the magnetic flux through the wire frame is Φ(t)=B L^2 cosθ=B L^2 cos(ωt). By Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the induced electromotive force ε=-dΦ/dt=B L^2 ω sin(ωt). The total resistance of the wire frame is R, so the instantaneous value of the induced current is i=ε/R=BL^2ωsin(ωt)/R. The applicable time range is 0≤ωt≤π/2.
